summary: Bhutan's Inheritance Act 1980 lets a person pass property by written or oral will, with shares for the family fixed by the Act when there is no will. Non-Bhutanese, including foreign spouses and children, cannot inherit land or houses and are shut out of any share of an inheritance. There is no trust or private foundation law.
family_claims: No court-ordered provision for dependants found. Without a will the Act sets the shares of family members in the main house (Ga 4, 5).
foreign_law_note: The Inheritance Act extends to all citizens and persons residing in Bhutan (Ga 1-3). Non-Bhutanese are not entitled to any share of an inheritance (Ga 2-11), and a foreign spouse and children of a Bhutanese may inherit only movables (Ga 6-23). I found no rule letting a foreign resident choose another law.
trust_note: Bhutan is not on the HCCH status table. I found no trust or private foundation statute. Civil society organisations are registered under the Civil Society Organizations Act, which is for non-profit purposes (not retrieved).
open_questions: The Act has not been checked for later amendments or for any protected share of children; a Bhutanese lawyer should confirm whether the will chapter (Ga 7) is subject to the family-share rules.
Confirm there is no trust statute and that no foundation law exists beyond the CSO Act.
